title: Scheme tests for finite stack maps, finite diagonals and finite-type atlases
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Use the fibred-groupoid, stack, algebraic-space and 2-fibre-product conventions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] and [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For a morphism $f:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ of categories over $\mathit{Sch}/S$, say that $f$ is representable finite if, for every $S$-scheme $T$ and map $t:h_T\to\mathcal G$, there are an $S$-scheme $Z$, a finite morphism $p:Z\to T$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and an equivalence $h_Z\simeq h_T\times_{\mathcal G}\mathcal F$ over $\mathit{Sch}/S$ identifying the first projection with $h_p$ up to a natural isomorphism over the identity of the base. Say that $\mathcal F$ has finite diagonal if, for all maps $h_T\to\mathcal F$ and $h_U\to\mathcal F$, the 2-fibre product is represented by $h_Z$, with both projections identified over the identity of the base with $h_p,h_q$ for morphisms $p:Z\to T$, $q:Z\to U$, and the induced morphism $Z\to T\times_S U$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is finite. Say that $\mathcal F$ admits a finite-type etale scheme atlas if there is an $S$-scheme $U$ whose structure morphism is locally of finite type and quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and a map $h_U\to\mathcal F$ all of whose scheme base changes are algebraic spaces with etale and surjective projections. Etaleness uses [def-weil-etale-morphism] and surjectivity is tested on etale scheme charts as in the recorded stack convention. Over a field, for a Deligne--Mumford stack, this is the finite-type atlas formulation of finite type; the empty atlas is allowed.
